symptoms: Signs of Instability: Hypotension, Acutely altered mental state, Signs of shock, Ischaemic chest discomfort, Acute heart failure.
Paediatric Bradycardia: HR < 60/min despite effective oxygenation and ventilation.

management_steps.details: Airway: open, maintain, protect. Breathing: oxygen if required (target sat 94-98%), ventilate if necessary. Circulation: assess pulse, BP, perfusion, attach ECG monitor. Drip: establish IV access. ECG Rhythm: 12 lead ECG, identify/treat underlying causes.

Atropine 1mg IV bolus (exclude hypoxia/hypothermia/head injury), repeat every 3-5 minutes up to 3mg. If Atropine ineffective: Adrenaline 2-10ug/min infusion (start at 0.05ug/kg/min and titrate) OR Transcutaneous Pacing. Consider alternatives: Transvenous pacing, High dose insulin (1U/kg if Beta Blocker or Ca Channel Blocker overdose), Glucagon.

Start CPR if HR < 60/min despite effective oxygenation and ventilation (1 Rescuer = 30:2, 2 Rescuers = 15:2). Adrenaline 0.1ml/kg IV of 1:10 000 dilution (Max dose 1mg) every 3-5 minutes. Atropine 0.02mg/kg IV if vagal tone or 1st deg AV block (Max dose 0.5mg). Consider pacing.

warnings: Exclude Hypoxia, Hypothermia, and Head Injury before administering Atropine in adult bradycardia.
